exposure: Care pathway (Cocoon midwifery-led birth center vs. traditional care pathway)
cohort: 984 women with low-risk pregnancies (590 in the Cocoon pathway and 394 in the traditional pathway) at a tertiary care hospital in Belgium from March 1, 2014, to February 29, 2016
finding: Women planning their births in the midwifery-led unit (Cocoon) experienced fewer interventions with no increase in adverse neonatal outcomes compared to those in the traditional care pathway.
mod_finding: Women with low-risk pregnancies who planned to give birth in a midwifery-led unit had lower rates of cesarean birth, induction, epidural analgesia, and episiotomy compared to those who chose traditional hospital care.
